newsitem.title: USA: A.H. Belo to buy Providence Journal.
newsitem.headline: A.H. Belo to buy Providence Journal.

text.p: A.H. Belo Corp and Providence Journal Co said on Thursday Belo agreed to acquire Providence Journal for $1.5 billion in cash and stock.
The merger would form one of the largest U.S. media companies with interests in publishing and broadcasting.
Providence Journal shareholders would receive $12.33 in cash and 0.5333 shars of Belo series A common stock for each share of Providence Journal, the companies said in a joint statement.
Belo and Providence Journal said the Providence Journal will become a wholly-owned subsidiary of Belo. Four directors from Providence Journal will join Belo's board, the companies said.
The deal will make Belo the eighth largest television group measured by revenues and the tenth largest in audience reach with the addition of Providence Journal's nine stations.
The combined company will have no overlapping television properties in the deal. The companies said they will own the Providence Journal-Bulletin and the Dallas Morning News.
The Providence Journal also owns interests in the Television Food Network and America's Health Network, both of which are cable television stations.
The deal would increase the number of Belo's total shares outstanding from 44.3 million to 69.7 million and the payment of $587 million in cash to Providence Journal holders, the companies said.

Providence Journal owns or manages 13 television stations in nine cities, while Belo owns six network affiliated stations. This does not include Belo's Seattle-Tacoma station, KIRO-TV, which would have to be divested under FCC regulations.
